senses.gloss: m. (כְּסַף) putting to shame; disgrace, shame.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Genesis 3:10">Targ. Y. Gen. III, 10</cite> (nakedness).
Targ. Ps. LXIX, 8 (fem.); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Horayot 13b:14">Hor. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>אתיא מילתא לידי כ׳</he> this may lead to putting (R. S.) to shame.
<cite ref="Taanit 9b:2">Taan. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>רחמנא … מכ׳ דשימי</he> the Lord save us from being put to shame through Shimi (by his questions).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 11a:2">Snh. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>מחמת כ׳</he> in order to save the man from shame.
<cite ref="Taanit 25a:1">Taan. 25ᵃ</cite> top <he>משום כ׳</he> to avoid exposure, v. <cite ref="A02910"><he>אַקְטַרְתָּא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 86b:13">B. Kam. 86ᵇ</cite> <he>כ׳</he> feeling of shame, contrad. to <cite ref="G00357"><he>זילותא</he></cite> disgrace though not felt.
Num. R. s. 14 בלשון ירושלמי … כס׳ in the Jerusalem dialect (of the Chaldaic) they say for ḥerpah, kissufa. [כיסופין Targ. Prov. II, 22 some ed., read: נסופין, v. סוּף II ch.]
